All Requirements for MBBS in Netherlands in 2026

Understand the essential criteria and requirements

Ensure your eligibility for pursuing MBBS and starting your medical journey.

Eligibility Criteria to Apply for MBBS in Netherlands 2026

To apply for MBBS admission in Netherlands, students must meet the following criteria:

  • Age should be 17 year by 31st December in Admission Year
  • Must have completed 10+2 education with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology as compulsory subjects.
  • A minimum of 70% to 75% in Physics, Chemistry, and Biology is required
  • 10+2 education must have been in an English-medium stream.
  • NEET should be qualified
  • University Entrance Exam

Required Documents for MBBS in Netherlands 2026

International students must send the following required documents for MBBS admission in the Netherlands.

10th Mark sheet 12th Mark sheet & Passing Certificate Transfer Certificate Birth Certificate Passport Aadhaar copy NEET result Sponsorship Affidavit 6 Month Bank Statement PCC (Police Clearance Certificate) 10 White Background Photographs with 70% Face (Size 3.5 X 4.5 CM) Recommendation Letters - 2 IELTS or TOEFL Result Statement of purpose Letter of Motivation (if possible) Medical certificate/HIV CV

Pathway Particulars

Duration of MBBS Course in Netherlands

MBBS in Netherlands follows a pattern with 6-7 years duration. The Netherlands does not follow the pattern used by the majority of the world but follows the European model of medical education with the following structure:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Medicine (3-year course): This is the pre-medical stage where students acquire core medical knowledge.
  • Master's in Medicine (3-year program): This phase involves hands-on practice and exposure within hospitals.
  • Internship & Licensing (1-2 years): After the master's program, students must undergo internships and pass the licensure exams for practice as doctors.

MBBS programs in Netherlands are extremely research-based, imparting quality medical education and hands-on experience and preparing students for medical professions globally.

Medium of Teaching

Most of the teaching language for medical programs in Netherlands is Dutch, with most being offered within the public universities. However, a few MBBS courses are offered in English within some universities, thereby making it accessible for international students. For students who wish to pursue Dutch-taught courses, a language proficiency test is required. For English-taught courses, proficiency in English (IELTS/TOEFL) is required.

Intake for MBBS Study

The MBBS admission in Netherlands typically follows two major intakes each year:

  • September Intake: The primary intake, with most universities accepting applications between October and April.
  • February Intake: A secondary intake available in limited universities, with applications open from July to November.

Since MBBS programs in Netherlands have limited seats, early application is highly recommended. International students must meet eligibility criteria, submit required documents, and apply through the university portal or centralized application systems like Studielink. Admission is competitive, especially in top medical colleges in Netherlands, so strong academic records and language proficiency (English or Dutch) are essential for selection.

Admission Procedure For Netherland MBBS College

A step-by-step roadmap to admission

  1. Fill out the admission form: Visit our official website https://www.rmcedu.com and complete the MBBS admission form with accurate details.
  2. Verification: The university will verify your application form, along with uploaded documents such as your passport, academic transcripts, and NEET scorecard, after you have submitted it.
  3. Screening: The university then undertakes a screening process in which the applicant must determine eligibility for admission to MBBS programs in Netherlands.
  4. University-Wise Admission Shortlist: After the completion of the screening, the university will publish a shortlist of selected students for admission.
  5. Visa Process: After shortlisting, the student should apply for a student visa to the nearest Netherlands Embassy or Consulate, attaching the confirmation of admission, passport, and other necessary documents.
  6. Physical Copy of Admission Letter: A hard copy of the admission letter will be sent by the university, which you will need to complete the visa process and enrollment.
  7. Fly to Netherlands: Book your tickets and travel to Netherlands to join your desired university.
  8. Complete enrollment once you reach there and start with your education.

Scholarships Offered for MBBS in Netherlands

Studying MBBS in Netherlands can prove to be costly, but various scholarships support international students with their expenses. The scholarships pay for tuition fees, living costs, or a combination of the two.

  • Holland Scholarship: Awarded for non-EU students, €5,000 for the initial study year.
  • Erasmus Mundus Scholarship: Provides scholarships for overseas students who are undertaking medical courses.
  • Orange Tulip Scholarship: Available for Indian students with partial or full fee scholarships.
  • University-Specific Scholarships: There are merit-based and need-based scholarships offered by most top medical schools.

Eligibility for the scholarship depends upon academic merit, entrance exam marks, and financial need. Early application increases the chances of securing financial aid.

MBBS Syllabus in Netherlands

Program phases and subjects covered

Year 1 (Pre-Clinical Phase)

Human Anatomy, Physiology, Biochemistry, Cell Biology, Genetics, Public Health, Medical Ethics, Introduction to Clinical Skills

Year 2 (Pre-Clinical Phase)

Pathology, Pharmacology, Microbiology, Immunology, Behavioral Sciences, Disease Mechanisms, Basic Diagnostics

Year 3 (Transition to Clinical Phase)

System-Based Study (Cardiology, Neurology, Gastroenterology, Respiratory System, Endocrinology), Evidence-Based Medicine, Communication Skills

Year 4 (Clinical Phase)

Internal Medicine, General Surgery, Pediatrics, Gynecology & Obstetrics, Psychiatry, Emergency Medicine, Family Medicine

Year 5 (Clinical Phase)

Orthopedics, ENT, Ophthalmology, Dermatology, Radiology, Anesthesiology, Neurology, Clinical Research Training

Year 6 (Internship / Clinical Rotations)

Full Clinical Rotations across all major departments including Internal Medicine, Surgery, Pediatrics, Gynecology, Emergency Medicine, and Elective Specializations
